summary: An L-4 lookout built in 1939 on McCart Peak in the Bitterroot National Forest, retired from fire duty in 1984, restored in 1991-92, and now a popular trail-in rental cabin.

facts.design: L-4, 14x14 ft live-in cab with catwalk on a low wooden tower (~10 ft)
facts.status_note: Restored 1991-92 after retirement from fire-watch duty in 1984; now a rental cabin

access.note: Reached only by a moderate 1.5-mile trail; no vehicle access; Forest Service rental cabin

visit.trail_note: 1.5-mile hike from the parking area; no snowmobiles, ATVs, or motorcycles on the trail

events.note: Built by the U.S. Forest Service; engineer Clyde Fickes
Retired from fire detection use, replaced by TeePee Lookout to the north
Completely restored 1991-92 by the Sula Ranger District, refitted to a 1940s appearance
Placed into the cabin rental program in 1993
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, May 1, 1994
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, June 19, 1996

evidence.supports: built 1939, restored 1991-92, retired 1984 and replaced by TeePee Lookout, placed in rental program 1993, popular with hikers
evidence.quote: Built by the U.S. Forest Service in 1939, McCart Lookout was completely restored in 1991-92 by the Sula Ranger District of the Bitterroot National Forest in Montana. The structure is an L-4, 14'x14' live-in cab with catwalk on a low wooden tower. It was used for fire detection until 1984 when it was replaced by TeePee Lookout to the north. Located on the edge of the Anaconda Pintler Wilderness and reached only by trail, McCart Lookout was placed in the cabin rental program in 1993 and has proven to be very popular with overnight hikers.

evidence.supports: built 1939, engineer Clyde Fickes, L-4 style, elevation ~7,115 ft, named for Bill McCart
evidence.quote: The McCart Fire Lookout , near Sula, Montana , was built in 1939. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1996.

evidence.supports: elevation and location near East Fork Forest Service Station
evidence.quote: It is an L-4 Fire Lookout, located at 7,115 feet (2,169 m) elevation, about 4 miles (6.4 km) south of the East Fork Forest Service Station in Bitterroot National Forest.

evidence.supports: named for Bill McCart, longtime Forest Service employee, East Fork (now Sula) District
evidence.quote: It was named for Bill McCart, a longtime National Forest Service employee in the East Fork District (now Sula District).

evidence.supports: location on McCart Peak east of Sula, edge of Anaconda-Pintler Wilderness, restored to 1940s appearance with stove, furniture, dishes
evidence.quote: McCart Lookout is a historic tower located on McCart Peak, east of Sula. It has been restored to reflect a lookout of the 1940s, including the stove, furniture, dishes and other small touches. It offers a unique chance for visitors to camp on a mountain peak, on the border of the Anaconda-Pintler Wilderness.

evidence.supports: cabin dimensions, sleeping capacity, catwalk, tower height, lack of water, access by 1.5-mile hike
evidence.quote: The lookout is a one room cabin with a bed platform suitable for two people. Bedding is not provided. The lookout can accommodate up to four. ... The lookout measures 14ft.X14ft. with a 30 inch catwalk around the outside. ... The lookout is built on a 10 foot tall tower, with narrow steps and catwalk. ... The tower is accessed by a moderate, 1.5-mile hike from the parking area.

evidence.supports: no vehicles/snowmobiles/ATVs on trail, horses allowed
evidence.quote: Snowmobiles and other off-road vehicles are not allowed on the trail, however, horses and other livestock are welcome.

notes_for_editor: The brief flags a register-number conflict ('They share a register number'), presumably with another lookout in the dataset; none of the three sources read here gave any indication McCart's NHLR number (US 85) is wrong, so this could not be resolved from these pages and should be checked against whichever other record shares the number.
